questions.q: Which of the following is another term used in art to refer to a pure colour?
questions.explain: Hue is the traditional colour name given to a specific wavelength of light (like 'red' or 'blue'). It refers to the pure state of a colour without black or white added.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: What defines 'Primary Colours' in traditional art and painting?
options: They are colours that have white added to them.
They are the darkest colours on the colour wheel.
They are basic colours that cannot be created by mixing other colours together.
They are colours that only exist in digital formats.
questions.explain: Primary colours are the fundamental building blocks in colour theory. In traditional pigment mixing (paint), they cannot be formed by mixing any other colours.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the three Primary Colours used in art?
questions.explain: In traditional art (pigment/paint mixing), the three primary colours are Red, Yellow, and Blue.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

options: By mixing a primary colour with black.
By mixing two primary colours together in equal proportions.
By adding water to a primary colour.
By mixing three primary colours together.
questions.explain: A secondary colour is created by equally mixing two primary colours. The three secondary colours are Green, Orange, and Violet (Purple).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which category of colours is formed by mixing one primary colour with one adjacent secondary colour on the colour wheel?
questions.explain: Tertiary colours (or intermediate colours) are created by mixing a primary colour with the secondary colour next to it on the colour wheel (e.g., Red-Orange).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Black, White, and Grey are not found on the standard colour wheel. They are categorized as:
questions.explain: Neutral colours do not have a strong hue and do not appear on the traditional colour wheel. They include black, white, grey, and sometimes brown and beige.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Colours such as Red, Orange, and Yellow are often grouped together and are known as:
questions.explain: Warm colours remind us of heat, sunshine, and fire. They are located on one half of the colour wheel and include red, orange, and yellow.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: What is the relationship between colours that are located directly opposite each other on the colour wheel?
questions.explain: Complementary colours sit opposite each other on the colour wheel (e.g., Red and Green). When placed side by side, they create high contrast and make each other look brighter.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: If a student wants to paint a sunset landscape to convey a feeling of warmth, which set of colours should they predominantly use?
questions.explain: Red, Orange, and Yellow are warm colours, perfectly suited for conveying the heat and visual atmosphere of a sunset.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Analogous colours are defined as colours that:
options: Are direct opposites on the colour wheel.
Sit side-by-side or adjacent to each other on the colour wheel.
Are exactly equal in visual weight.
questions.explain: Analogous colours are groups of three colours that are next to each other on the colour wheel (e.g., Red, Red-Orange, and Orange). They share a common hue and create a harmonious, unified look.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
